title: QBR - Vela Systems Health Check
summary: Quarterly health check covering usage trends, cost drivers, recent incidents, roadmap alignment, and next steps for expanding Dedicated capacity pilot. Customer is generally happy with latency but wants cost optimization and clearer rollout timeline for VPC/private features.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-12-05
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen, Ethan Park, Priya Rao (Redwood) -- Liam O'Connor, Sofia Martinez, Raj Patel, Amira Khan (Vela Systems)
---
[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining the QBR for Vela, um we appreciate you taking time. quick agenda: usage/costs, any reliability incidents, roadmap asks, and action items. priya will kick off with adoption notes.
[00:22] Priya Rao: hey all, quick intro, we've seen steady embed/ gen usage this quarter — total tokens up about 42% month over month since August, embeddings up 30%. biggest driver is the new search rerank feature you shipped in sept.
[00:38] Liam O'Connor: yeah that's been huge, the search relevancy uptick is noticeable. cost though, it's creeping up; we circled back to finance and they flagged the average cost per 1k tokens is higher than we projected.
[00:52] Ethan Park: totally understand. do you have the breakdown between hosted API usage vs dedicated pilot? That helps pinpoint where batching/quantization could help.
[01:05] Sofia Martinez: 80% hosted, 20% dedicated pilot. dedicated is our prod-ish path but it's limited to the chat endpoints. the hosted bursts are mostly for nightly reindexing and some user-facing analytics.
[01:22] Maya Chen: ok that maps to the cost delta — hosted has variable unit cost. we suggested in october a batching profile and prefix caching for reindexing jobs; did you get a chance to try the suggested batch size change?
[01:36] Sofia Martinez: we tried bumping batch to 256 for embeddings but saw latency spikes during peak; turned it back down to 128. maybe we configured it wrong, or the KV cache wasn't engaged.
[01:50] Ethan Park: got it. could be the KV cache TTL or the way the reindex job opens parallel connections. we can run a quick benchmark with your workload and tune the kernel selection / batch mix — that's something we can do as a follow-up bench.
[02:05] Raj Patel: on reliability, we had an incident in mid-november where a regional failover caused a 12-minute degradation in responses for our EMEA users. we filed an incident with your support and got a postmortem but wanted to understand root cause more — was that the autoscaling bug you mentioned?
[02:22] Priya Rao: yes that was related to an edge case in the autoscaler when combined with a very bursty token distribution — it under-provisioned a few Dedicated nodes and the routing fallback to hosted added latency. the engineering team rolled a fix Nov 20 and we haven't seen a recurrence. transcription note: "autoscaler" was sometimes transcribed as "auto scaler" in logs.
[02:42] Liam O'Connor: the postmortem was helpful, but can we get guaranteed SLO improvements for EMEA? our SLAs with customers demand <250ms p95 for chat. right now you're hovering ~300ms at peak.
[02:55] Ethan Park: for p95 under 250ms we'd recommend moving more of the user-facing endpoints to Dedicated capacity and enabling region pinning. that, plus prefix caching for common prompts, should bring latency down. tradeoff is cost — Dedicated commit will cost more upfront but reduces per-token cost at scale.
[03:18] Amira Khan: timeline question — when will the VPC private deployment GA? we need VPC for data residency and to connect to our internal KMS.
[03:28] Maya Chen: VPC private GA is projected for Q1 2026. there are two tracks: managed VPC (control plane still on Redwood) and on-prem package. both support KMS integration; managed VPC will be first. rough dates but we'll share the formal roadmap doc.
[03:43] Sofia Martinez: ok that's helpful. does managed VPC include SAML SSO and audit logs? compliance team asked specifically about SOC2 scope extension.
[03:52] Priya Rao: yes SSO/SAML and RBAC are in the private feature set; SOC2 controls for customer logs and longer retention options are part of the enterprise package. I'll attach the compliance pack after the call.
[04:05] Liam O'Connor: another ask — our legal team wants a data flow diagram and encryption at rest details, especially how KMS keys are used and whether Redwood has access.
[04:18] Maya Chen: short answer: with managed VPC you bring your KMS keys and Redwood doesn't hold plaintext, and access is limited; I'll get the architecture diagram and the KMS FAQ.
[04:29] Raj Patel: on the product roadmap, any upcoming features around quantized model variants? we've heard about 4-bit quantization improving cost without too much perf loss.
[04:40] Ethan Park: yes, the runtime team has been rolling out quantization profiles — 4-bit mixed FP16 paths for specific models. for those we provide perf vs quality deltas and can recommend which to use per route. we can run evals on your prompts. note: sometimes spec names get transcribed weirdly, e.g., "4bit" -> "forty-bit" in automated minutes, haha.
[04:59] Amira Khan: would be great if you can run the evals on our top-100 prompts to measure hallucination/regression risk.
[05:09] Priya Rao: noted. we'll schedule an eval run.
[05:14] Liam O'Connor: pricing: can you re-run the committed capacity pricing for us if we move 50% of peak traffic to Dedicated? finance needs a three-year TCO projection.
[05:26] Maya Chen: yes — ethan and I can put together a TCO model. we'll factor in reserved monthly commit discounts, projected token growth, and bundling of observability retention.
[05:38] Sofia Martinez: FYI we also want better per-route cost dashboards. the current console shows token breakdown but not a nice split by feature flag.
[05:48] Priya Rao: we do have a per-route cost beta. I'll enable it for your account and schedule a walkthrough.
[05:58] [06:00] Liam O'Connor: little thing — sometimes the console's embedding unit metrics are off (e.g., counting each dimension as a unit) — is that a known telemetry bug?
[06:12] Ethan Park: we saw a telemetry mismatch in Sept; should be fixed but we'll double-check the account-level metrics and reconcile with billing.
[06:22] Maya Chen: quick check-in on actionables: we have bench, evals, compliance pack, TCO, per-route beta. anything else?
[06:32] Amira Khan: can you also share the recommended prompt prefixes for caching? engineering wants the examples.
[06:38] Priya Rao: yes, prompt prefix patterns and caching guidance will be in the follow-up doc.
[06:43] [06:50] Raj Patel: security — do you support customer-managed encryption keys (CMK) in the managed VPC? I mean HSM-backed keys?
[06:53] Maya Chen: yes CMKs with HSM are supported in the managed VPC; detail will be in the compliance packet.
[07:02] Liam O'Connor: one more ops ask: during the November incident our support SLA was fine but we'd like a named escalation path for P1s. can we get a dedicated channel?
[07:12] Priya Rao: absolutely — i'll add a P1 escalation contact and set up a dedicated slack channel with on-call rotation.
[07:20] Ethan Park: on the bench — if we run the workload sim, we'll need a dataset dump or representative prompt set. do you prefer us to use masked data or a synthetic corpus?
[07:31] Sofia Martinez: masked production prompts would be best. we can scrub PII and provide them.
[07:37] Maya Chen: perfect. we'll sync on secure transfer method; s3 with temporary creds or the Vela SFTP.
[07:44] [07:55] Priya Rao: ok moving toward close — recap of next steps and owners.
[08:00] Maya Chen: recap: 1) Bench run for batching/kv cache tuning (Ethan + Vela eng) 2) Top-100 prompt evals for quantization quality (Priya + SE) 3) TCO for 50% Dedicated migration (Maya + Ethan) 4) Compliance pack + architecture/KMS doc (Maya) 5) Enable per-route cost beta and walkthrough (Priya) 6) P1 escalation & dedicated channel (Priya) 7) Reconcile telemetry/billing numbers (Ethan)
[08:40] Amira Khan: timeline expectations? can we get first drafts in two weeks?
[08:47] Maya Chen: yes two weeks for the bench plan and compliance packet draft; TCO within three weeks. will follow up with calendar invites.
[08:58] Raj Patel: thanks everyone, appreciate the partnership.
[09:03] Maya Chen: thanks all. ending call.
---
End of transcript. Note: audio transcription included periods of overlap and minor name misrecognitions (e.g., "Vela" occasionally as "Veller").
